title: Data-Driven Exploration of Synthesizable Strained Hydrocarbons as High-Energy-Density Candidates for Sustainable Aviation Fuels
image_alt: Placeholder graphic for the sustainable aviation-fuel research story
story: This work asks how a vast hydrocarbon space can be narrowed to useful high-energy-density fuel candidates without ignoring whether the molecules could realistically be made. A LEGO-based generation strategy assembled strained hydrocarbon frameworks from molecular building blocks, after which data-driven property prediction and computational screening prioritized promising structures. The study connects systematic chemical-space generation with synthesizability-aware molecular design for sustainable aviation fuels.

title: Chemical Space Exploration of Organic Donor-Acceptor TADF Emitters and Molecular Design
image_alt: Placeholder graphic for the TADF emitter research story
story: This study explores how donor and acceptor fragments can be recombined systematically to move beyond a small set of familiar TADF molecules. The LEGO-based strategy generated a wider donor–acceptor chemical space, while computed properties and multi-objective screening were used to identify balanced candidates. The resulting workflow turns fragment recombination into a reproducible molecular-design process for organic emitters.

title: From Knowledge to Action: Outcomes of the 2025 Large Language Models Hackathon for Applications in Materials Science and Chemistry
image_alt: Placeholder graphic for the LLM hackathon research story
story: This collaborative work documents what happens when large language models are tested on practical problems in materials science and chemistry. The hackathon moved from discussion to working prototypes and exposed both useful capabilities and limitations of scientific LLM workflows. It provides a community snapshot of how language-model systems can help translate scientific knowledge into computational action.

title: Computational Exploration of Small Hydrocarbon Networks: A Stochastic Generation and DFT Refinement Framework
authors: Sandip Giri; S. Satpati; Tarun Roy; S. Ghosal; A. Anoop
image_alt: Placeholder graphic for the hydrocarbon-network research story
story: The central problem is the enormous number of possible small hydrocarbon structures, many of which are missed by intuition-led enumeration. A stochastic generation framework created candidate networks by connecting molecular fragments, and density-functional theory then refined and evaluated the generated structures. The project established a reusable route from automated structure generation to quantum-chemical validation and the HydroMol exploration interface.

title: Exploring the Chemical Space of Non-Covalent Molecular Clusters using Automated Cluster Building Algorithm and Neural Network Potential
image_alt: Placeholder graphic for the molecular-cluster research story
story: Non-covalent clusters have broad configurational spaces because molecular identity, orientation, and packing all vary together. This work combined automated cluster building with a neural-network potential to generate and assess candidates more efficiently than direct high-level calculations alone. The resulting workflow extends chemical-space exploration from covalent molecules to weakly bound molecular assemblies.

title: Computational Investigation of Meso-Substituted, Heavy Atom-Free BODIPY Derivatives as Photosensitizers: Insights From TDDFT and Dynamics Studies
authors: M. Banerjee; Sandip Giri; A. Anoop
image_alt: Placeholder graphic for the BODIPY photosensitizer research story
story: This paper investigates how meso substitution changes the excited-state behaviour of heavy-atom-free BODIPY photosensitizers. Time-dependent density-functional theory and dynamics calculations were used to connect molecular structure with electronic states and relaxation pathways. The analysis provides mechanistic guidance for designing photosensitizers without relying on heavy atoms.

title: Exploring the Conformational Space of a Sulfonyl-Based Ionic Liquid on Platinum-Based Mono and Bimetallic Surfaces
authors: A. P. Sarkar; R. Sahu; Sandip Giri; A. Anoop; S. K. Reddy
image_alt: Placeholder graphic for the ionic-liquid surface research story
story: An ionic liquid near a metal surface can adopt many competing arrangements, making a single optimized structure an incomplete description. This study explored the conformational space of a sulfonyl-based ionic liquid on platinum-based mono- and bimetallic surfaces and compared the resulting adsorption motifs. The work shows why systematic configurational sampling is important for understanding molecular interfaces.

title: Hydrogen Bond-Assisted Excited State Switching and Fluoride Responsive Behavior of Orthogonal Spiroborate Ester Derived from Naturally Occurring α-Mangostin
authors: S. U. Saraswathy; L. C. Lalithabai; Sandip Giri; S. Ayoob; S. Haleema; A. Anoop; S. Sumalekshmy
image_alt: Placeholder graphic for the spiroborate switching research story
story: This study examines how hydrogen bonding and fluoride binding influence the excited-state response of an orthogonal spiroborate ester derived from α-mangostin. Experiment and computation were used to interpret the switching behaviour and connect molecular interactions to the observed optical response. The work illustrates how targeted electronic-structure analysis can explain responsive molecular systems.

title: Selective synthesis of the missing tiara-like Ni10, Ni5, and Ni6 thiolates by the C–S bond cleavage of bis(thioether) molecules with a DFT study
authors: S. Debnath; Sandip Giri; G. Mani
image_alt: Placeholder graphic for the nickel-thiolate research story
story: The paper addresses the selective formation of previously missing tiara-like nickel thiolate clusters produced through carbon–sulfur bond cleavage. Structural characterization was paired with density-functional theory to examine the stability and bonding of the Ni10, Ni5, and Ni6 products. The computational contribution helps connect the observed synthetic selectivity with the electronic structure of these metal clusters.
